submissionAttempts.body:
CONCLUSION
The observation cursor for this workspace's Ordarium integration is a global, filter-independent durable position — NOT per-subscription. The claim in docs/engineering/notes/cursor-note.md ("cursor positions are per-subscription, not global") does not apply.

EVIDENCE
1) What this workspace integrates. Palimpsest consumes Ordarium; the dependency manifests pin the Ordarium release line v1.3.1 (package.json dependencies + pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides), and the installed artifacts match: node_modules/@ordarium/core|ledger-sqlite|host-kit/package.json all read 1.3.1. The state-kind integration is createStateStore({runtime}) exposed as PalimpsestEffectsRuntime.state (src/effects/runtime.ts:124) and consumed in src/telemetry/state_persistence.ts, which pages via store.list({namespace}, cursor) / page.nextCursor.

2) The two competing statements about the same proposition (is the observation cursor global or per-subscription?):
- Informational note (docs/engineering/notes/cursor-note.md): says per-subscription; self-declares "informational, not normative" and "was not updated against the current pinned artifact".
- Pinned Ordarium v1.3.1 shipped contract (level-1 source):
  * @ordarium/core dist/src/types.d.ts — StateChangePage.cursor: "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change"; StateChangeFeed is "incremental observation of committed state revisions after a durable position (ORD-BOOT-0)".
  * @ordarium/ledger-sqlite dist/src/index.js, changes(): "Semantic validation against the global high-water mark (ORD-BOOT-0.1): the cursor is a global, filter-independent position, so this compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence." A position beyond that mark raises InvalidCursorError.
  * @ordarium/core dist/src/ledger.js, MemoryLedger.changes(): commit positions are a single contiguous 1..n sequence across ALL namespaces; the namespace filter only skips entries when building a page, it never rebases or re-scopes the cursor.
  * @ordarium/core dist/src/errors.d.ts, InvalidCursorError: a cursor not decodable as a durable position "fails closed instead of silently restarting from the beginning of the feed."
  * The list-pagination cursors (`nextCursor?` on list/listStates/stateHistory) are likewise opaque positions in the ledger's global ordering; the filter is applied orthogonally to the position, not baked into it.

3) Rule applied (docs/engineering/08-source-precedence-policy.md): (1) the published contract of the exact pinned version (shipped type declarations and release specification) governs that interface's behaviour; (2) the project's normative spec governs project-internal semantics; (3) informational records — engineering notes, historical alignment records — are explanatory only and NEVER override 1 or 2. The cursor-note is a level-3 record and on its own face stale against the pin; the pinned 1.3.1 artifact is level-1. Therefore the global/filter-independent behaviour applies and the note is void as to this question. (Provenance nuance: docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md's latest entries still record the pin as 1.2.0 — a historical record stale against the actual manifests; it does not change which artifact is the exact pin. The exact pinned version is 1.3.1.)

CONSEQUENCES FOR THE INTEGRATION
- The cursor is a position in one global commit order, not scoped to the subscription/filter that emitted it. Reusing it under a different namespace filter is well-defined; a filter change must not be treated as making the cursor invalid.
- The only rejection case is a position beyond the ledger's global high-water mark (foreign/restored/replaced/corrupt ledger), which fails closed with InvalidCursorError — never a silent restart from zero.
- The change-feed cursor is always present, even at the end of the feed (durable resume position); list `nextCursor?` cursors are pagination-only and absent at the end.
- The workspace's actual consumption (src/telemetry/state_persistence.ts: fixed namespace, fresh start each load, no cross-filter cursor reuse) is compatible with this contract; it does not consume the change feed at all (zero occurrences of changes/supportsStateChangeFeed/stateChangeFeed in src/). Palimpsest's own graph.project.cursor / viewCursor are project-internal event-position/view-freshness fields (docs/engineering/35) — a different concept, not in conflict.

NO CROSS-REPO ESCALATION NEEDED
The conflict is between a level-1 shipped artifact (Ordarium's own published contract, which docs/engineering/07 §0 designates as the owning project's authority) and a level-3 note that is explicitly non-normative and flagged stale. The local source-precedence rule plus the note's own staleness disclaimer resolve it deterministically, so no peer contact was warranted.
